$comment: Names an artifact writer must survive: test class and method names that reach the filesystem. See README.md.

cases.description: the well-formed baseline every other case is a mutation of
an empty name, which resolves to no path segment at all
a name that is only spaces - legible in a listing, unusable as a path
a name that resolves to the current or parent directory
a name that walks out of the output directory
a POSIX separator inside a name, which would write into a subdirectory
the Windows separator, which is also a legal POSIX file-name character
a NUL inside a name - InvalidPathException before any byte is written
a line break inside a name, which forges a line in any listing
a lone high surrogate: encodes to no bytes, so the path cannot be built
a well-formed surrogate pair, which truncation must not split
U+FFFE and U+FFFF in a name - legal UTF-8 bytes that some filesystems refuse
a bidi override in a name, so a listing reads backwards from there
the longest name that still leaves room for the longest artifact suffix
exactly the per-component limit, so any suffix pushes it over
one byte past the per-component limit every mainstream filesystem shares
a name four times the component limit
a name at PATH_MAX, so even the directory it names cannot be created
two hundred three-byte characters: under the limit in characters, over it in bytes, which is where a character-counting cap fails
a long name of surrogate pairs, so a byte-counting cap must still land on a character boundary
over-long and carrying a separator, so neither guard may hide the other
